guidance.summary: Meta guided Q3 2026 revenue to $61-64 billion, raised the low end of full-year 2026 total expenses to $165-169 billion, expects 2026 operating income above 2025, narrowed 2026 capex to $130-145 billion, and raised its remaining-2026 tax rate outlook to 15-17%.

guidance.sentence: We expect third quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $61-64 billion.
Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.
We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $165-169 billion.
We continue to expect to deliver operating income this year that is above 2025 operating income.
We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $130-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $125-145 billion.
Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our tax rate for the remaining quarters of 2026 to be between 15-17%, an increase from our prior outlook of 13-16%.

writeup.headline: Meta rates Hold at 64, one point below Buy, as strong fundamentals meet a rich valuation.
writeup.thesis: Meta scores 64, a Hold with high confidence, just 1 point short of the Buy threshold at 65. The business side is strong: balance sheet scores 93 (cash covers debt 1.08 times, net debt to FCF of -0.16), quality scores 79 on an 81.75% gross margin and 38.08% operating margin, and growth scores 70 with revenue up 27.96% year on year in the latest quarter. Valuation is the main drag at 29: price to FCF of 46.186 sits in the 99.2nd percentile of its own history, and the FCF yield is 3.045 points below the 10-year Treasury yield, partly because heavy AI spending holds the FCF margin to 17.95%. Trend (65) and news risk (59) are middling: the price is 16.82% above its 200-day average, but 12-1 month momentum is -6.11% and it lags QQQ by 4.61 points, while news was mildly positive on broker target raises and the smart-glasses launch at Connect.
key_risks: AI capex: the early-warning check is AMBER at 6/18, with 2026 capex guided to $130-145B weighing on free cash flow.
Valuation is stretched on cash flow, with price to FCF at the 99.2nd percentile of its history.
Revenue growth is slowing, down 5.12 percentage points from the prior pace.
Regulatory overhang: the FTC is appealing to revive its antitrust case, and youth-harm trials are still ahead.
Stock-based compensation runs at 11.01% of revenue.
what_would_change: A 1-point gain in the composite score would lift the rating to Buy, for example from stronger Q3 results on October 21, firmer momentum or better news.
A rise in free cash flow, or a lower price, would improve the valuation score of 29, which is the biggest drag.
The rating would fall to Sell only if the score dropped 20 points to below 45, which would likely take a sharp drop in growth or a much worse capex warning.
If the capex early warning moved from AMBER to a more severe level, the rating could be capped.
